clippings.speaker: Keanu Reeves
clippings.quote: One day I got an email from Lana, “How’s it going? I’m thinking about…” And I was like, “What!?” Then, it was a conversation—she shared with me some of what was happening with her personally, and what had brought her to a place of telling a story with The Matrix. And she asked me how I would feel about it. “YES.” On these films, with Lana, it’s “YES.”
clippings.title: It was a “YES” when Keanu Reeves was asked to return to The Matrix
clippings.context: Q&A ahead of The Matrix Resurrections' release, on being asked back to play Neo.

clippings.speaker: Keanu Reeves
clippings.quote: So, my experience [of the trilogy] was with her behind a monitor, now she’s in front—of course, she’ll reference the monitor. Her evolution as a filmmaker is extraordinary. So, what we have now is an artist who’s interested in natural light, who wants to be next to the camera and literally connects herself to the camera and becomes this other thing, which I’ve never seen before.
clippings.title: It was a “YES” when Keanu Reeves was asked to return to The Matrix
clippings.context: Same Q&A, asked how Lana had evolved as a filmmaker since the original trilogy.

clippings.speaker: Keanu Reeves
clippings.quote: You can go to either of them and ask a question and much more often than not they’ll agree and tell you the same thing. They are independent and together.
clippings.title: Filmmaking Wachowski brothers hide in the shadows of ‘The Matrix’
clippings.context: Profile of the then-press-shy Wachowskis at the release of The Matrix Reloaded; Reeves speaks of the two siblings together.

clippings.speaker: Keanu Reeves
clippings.quote: They’re one of the most sensitive people I’ve ever met.
clippings.title: Filmmaking Wachowski brothers hide in the shadows of ‘The Matrix’
clippings.context: Same 2003 profile; Reeves describing the Wachowski siblings as almost a single person.

clippings.speaker: Lana Wachowski
clippings.quote: We showed the film to Keanu, and he really was blown away by it, and he said something that was typically Keanu, where it’s incredibly insightful. He’s just sort of sitting there, and you don’t expect some incredible revelation to come out of him at that moment, like casual brilliance just kind of rolls off of Keanu.
clippings.title: The Matrix 4 “Describes the Next 20 Years of Digital Life”
clippings.context: Said on a panel at the Berlin International Literature Festival with co-writers Aleksandar Hemon and David Mitchell, reported by Den of Geek.

clippings.speaker: Lana Wachowski
clippings.quote: How do you tell an actor that they’re going to have to spend four months training and learning Kung Fu when they could make another movie in that same time? That’s what impressed us about Keanu. He understood why it was necessary and the dedication it required.
clippings.title: The Making of The Matrix
clippings.context: Joint statement credited to both Wachowskis (Lana then credited as Larry) in the studio's 1999 production notes.

clippings.speaker: Lana Wachowski
clippings.quote: Keanu did some amazing work in this scene which included 6 hours every morning of prosthetic makeup. And he had to sit in a freezing cold vat of goo for another six hours..
clippings.title: Chat Transcript: Wachowski Brothers
clippings.context: Live online chat during a screening of The Matrix; answers are credited jointly to 'WachowskiBros', commenting on the pod scene.
